quest.title: Lasting Promise
quest.description: Having prepared the gifts, you travel together to the place where "Tsubaki" lives.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x525, Mora x35475, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x8

chapter.title: The Whispers of the Crane and the White Rabbit

talks.objective: Head over to the designated area recorded in the notebook

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So a transcendent being lives here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Brr... If someone lives here, then why is it so chilly?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Hmm... I'm asking myself the same question...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: How strange, I'm quite sure that this is the location my mother wrote about, but... surely...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hmm... I'm starting to have second thoughts...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: But, since we're here, I still think we should go inside and explore in full.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, makes sense. Who knows, maybe there's a surprise waiting in there for us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, um... what does the notebook say, exactly?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Let me think...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: "A crane brings <color=#00E1FFFF>1</color> fresh flower in its beak to decorate my hair, while a white rabbit sews a hemline from <color=#00E1FFFF>4</color> rays of moonlight. Dressed appropriately, I face <color=#00E1FFFF>eastward</color> and call out Tsubaki's name <color=#00E1FFFF>7</color> times. In the blink of an eye, I am standing on the path that leads to her house."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like a fairytale... So your mom would do a little ritual and just like that, Tsubaki would come to meet her?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It does sound a lot like an adeptus, actually.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I have a feeling that it could be some sort of code...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Let's get a little closer before coming to any conclusions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Good idea!

choices.text: Maybe Tsubaki really is a fox envoy?

talks.objective: Search for suspicious places based on the hints

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: *sigh* Here will do just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, let's see what the notebook says!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon bets it's all about mysterious treasure! Ah, so exciting!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Psst, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? Why are you whispering all of a sudden? You're making Paimon nervous...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Come with me. Let's go over there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhhh, you want to let Ayaka read the notebook without distraction. Seems whatever's written in there must be pretty major after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But, um, based on her expression... probably not a treasure map.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, what could it be?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: *long exhale*

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Traveler, Paimon, sorry to keep you waiting so long.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No worries, it wasn't long at all! You're a very fast reader.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Have you finished reading the notebook?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Yes, I have.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I think I ought to share the truth of this notebook with you both.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Even though the contents are completely different than what I was expecting...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Different how? You mean, it wasn't a fox envoy who wrote this?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Not a fox envoy, no.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: It turns out that Tsubaki's real identity...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: ...is my mother herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh!?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Surprised? M—Me too... But that's what it says at the very beginning of the notebook.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Ahem... "Tsubaki and I are the same person, and yet we are different. When I become Tsubaki, I stop being Kamisato Kayo and become the most ordinary woman in the world."

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: "What follows in these pages is the ordinary, everyday life of a regular person. Nothing more, nothing less."

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: This notebook is, for the most part, a collection of my mother's musings, both private and trivial. All of the things we thought were about Tsubaki... were in fact about my mother herself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... that means that the kimono design, and the international dishes...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Are things that my mother wished to try, yes.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I'm sure this all sounds utterly bizarre to you, but to me at least, my mother's behavior is completely understandable.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Or to put it another way, I... I—I actually have another side to myself as well.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I was at a loss for words when I started reading the contents of the notebook... It almost felt like... like someone had looked inside my mind, examined my thoughts, and then written them all down on paper...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ayaka...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: From the moment my mother married my father, she became the mother of the Kamisato household, and with that came all sorts of duties. At the same time, the prestige of the Yashiro Commission brought its own share of responsibility.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: On top of that, every action she ever took was seen as representing the Kamisato Clan. People were always watching her. Under such circumstances, she never had much time to do the things she really wanted to do.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: After my parents passed away, Ayato and I took over responsibility for the affairs of the clan. We ran into all sorts of difficulties during that time... I'm not sure if people outside the clan could ever imagine what it was like.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Every time I found myself up against a difficult issue, I'd ask myself: Did my mother go through this, too? What would she have done in this situation?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Maybe it's because it'd been so long since I last saw her, but... somehow, all that was left of her in my mind was the side of her that inspired awe and commanded respect...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: But... my image of her was incorrect.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: When I read this notebook, I realized... She was just like me. Underneath whatever position she may have held, she was just an ordinary person.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: She liked pretty kimonos, she wanted to try food from different places, she yearned to see sights she'd never seen before...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Maybe this all sounds immature to you, but... I feel just the same way. I want to live life not as Kamisato Ayaka, but as an ordinary woman.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Mother wrote that she'd always wanted to go to a local Inazuman festival. She said that sometimes, on a clear night, if you looked out from our house, you could see lights off in the distance.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I've seen those lights too! It looks so lively with so many people — and it's so brightly lit it makes the whole sky glow... Of course, sometimes it does make me a bit anxious from a public order perspective.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: But for someone of my position to just show up at a festival with no warning — it could be considered improper etiquette. Especially in my parents' generation, when the Yashiro Commission didn't have a particularly close relationship with the populace...

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Even if no one stopped us, the idea of the Yashiro Commission going out into the crowd... It'd certainly draw some strange looks. People would probably start thinking there was trouble afoot.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Mother said that she didn't want to put people on edge — she wanted everyone to enjoy the fun and freedom of the festival... She didn't want to disturb them, and didn't have much free time anyway, so she never went. Not even once.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw... So the kimono design — that must have been the outfit she planned on wearing if she ever did go to a festival, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: That's right. And sometimes, festivals sell international food. She wanted to try that, too.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: I hope this isn't a disrespectful thing to say, but... I never knew my mother was so in touch with her inner child, haha.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's not disrespectful at all! Paimon thinks your mom was the best of both — a big softie on the inside and a big sense of responsibility on the outside!

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Without knowing it, I've ended up fulfilling several of my mother's wishes already. *sigh* But going to a festival is the one thing that I cannot do for her.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Perhaps this is one thing that can simply never be.

choices.text: You've already achieved so many things.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I understand.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: ...Thank you. I think I realize something now.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Mother and I are so similar in so many ways. The things she faced are things that I too will go on to face.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: She chose to place her unfulfilled wishes onto the identity of Tsubaki. As for me... I've already decided.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh! So you've decided on an alter ego too?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: No, um...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I don't plan to do anything like that. I think... I think I will set myself a new goal: To live each day without regrets.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: So, um... Traveler, I... Ahem...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Whew, deep breaths, Ayaka, deep breaths...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: *sigh* Would you be at all interested in checking out an Inazuman festival?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's been dying to go ever since we saw that poster! Paimon would love to go with you Ayaka!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So, you've really never been to a festival?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hey, come on, don't make fun! It's just because I used to have the same concerns that my mother did... but now, I think I don't need to worry about it so much.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I'm going to be true to myself and fulfill the wish that my mother and I shared. I know that you of all people can understand me going my own way on this...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: So... let's do this, you and me! Let's go to a festival together!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'd love to join you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wants to come! Festivals here have loads of tasty snacks too, right? Oh, and fun and games? Hee-hee!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: ...Great! Thanks, you guys!

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: If we head over now, we should still make it in time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, good point, today's the last day, right? What are we waiting for — let's go!

choices.text: It's not your fault, it's just the way things are.

talks.objective: Investigate the shrubbery on the stone wall

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Knock seven times

dialogues.speaker: Conspicuous Stone Wall
dialogues.text: Some strange sounds can be heard coming from within the stone wall.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Did it open, did it open? Did our "Inazumadeptus" leave any treasure here?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: What's this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh... Looks like a book.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: It seems to be another notebook.

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Could it be Tsubaki's notebook...?

dialogues.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
dialogues.text: Let's step back outside now. The atmosphere here is different than I'd imagined. Somehow... it makes me a little reluctant to open the notebook.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knows what you mean — reading in low light is really bad for your eyes. C'mon, let's get back outside!

talks.objective: Go outside the cave to check the notebook
